programme.title: Como Dice el Dicho

programme.title: Como Dice el Dicho

programme.title: Como Dice el Dicho

programme.title: Como Dice el Dicho

programme.title: Spring of Changdeokgung Palace: A Feast of Spring Flowers
programme.desc: Built during King Taejong’s reign, Changdeokgung Palace was originally constructed as a secondary palace but served as the main palace for a longer period. programme.title: Creating Folding Screens: Pasting Master
programme.desc: Baechup is the traditional Korean technique for mounting calligraphy and paintings to enhance their preservation and beauty. Appreciate the master's craftmanship as he create a traditional ten-panel folding screen. (Provided by Korea Heritage Service, Korea Heritage Agency, K-Heritage Channel)

programme.title: Echoes of a Thousand Years: Musical Instrument Master
programme.desc: At the heart of Korean rhythm is the janggu, the traditional hourglass drum. From wood shaping to skin tightening, each step carries a legacy of sound and craftsmanship. (Provided by Korea Heritage Service, Korea Heritage Agency, K-Heritage Channel)

programme.title: Rising with the Wind: Kite Making Master
programme.desc: Paper and bamboo come together in the hands of a skilled artisan to create a traditional kite. Every cut and brushstroke carries care, as the kite soars with hopes into the sky. (Provided by Korea Heritage Service, Korea Heritage Agency, K-Heritage Channel)

programme.title: The Beauty of Patience: Ottchil Master
programme.desc: A Ottchil Master is an artisan skilled in decorating objects and furniture surfaces beautifully with ottchil (natural varnish/lacquer) and shells. Appreciate the works filled with the dedication and patience of the Lacquerware Master. (Provided by Korea Heritage Service, Korea Heritage Agency, K-Heritage Channel)

programme.title: A Bowl Made by the Sea: Tongyeong Neomul Bibimbap
programme.desc: There are various regional versions of traditional bibimbap, but Tongyeong's version is accompanied by tofu soup. Experience the special bibimbap of Tongyeong. (Provided by Korea Heritage Service, Korea Heritage Agency, K-Heritage Channel)

programme.title: Creating a Four-Legged Table: Wooden Furniture Master
programme.desc: Carpenters are artisans who make windows, woodenware, and wooden furniture. They continue the traditional woodworking techniques, creating works like the Sabangtakja (four-sided table). Appreciate the works of Carpenters. (Provided by Korea Heritage Service, Korea Heritage Agency, K-Heritage Channel)

programme.title: The Way of the Scholar: Nakjukjangdo
programme.desc: Jangdo is a small knife carried on the body for daily use, self-defense, or as an ornament. Nakjukjangdo is a traditional knife made using the Nakjuk technique. Appreciate Nakjukjangdo, used while walking the path of scholars. (Provided by Korea Heritage Service, Korea Heritage Agency, K-Heritage Channel)

programme.title: Embodying Wishes in Paper: Jihwa Master
programme.desc: Jihwa has been used not only in the royal court but also in family celebrations, Buddhist ceremonies, and shamanic rituals since ancient times. A Jihwa master is an artisan who cuts and decorates paper to create adornments for ceremonies. (Provided by Korea Heritage Service, Korea Heritage Agency, K-Heritage Channel)

programme.title: Spring of Changdeokgung Palace: A Feast of Spring Flowers
programme.desc: Built during King Taejong’s reign, Changdeokgung Palace was originally constructed as a secondary palace but served as the main palace for a longer period. programme.title: Peaceful Mudflats: Reed Swaying in the Wind, Suncheon Bay
programme.desc: Located on the southern coast, Suncheon Bay features stunning reed fields and Salicornia (glasswort) colonies. It is home to diverse tidal flat creatures and rare birds like the black-faced spoonbill. (Provided by Korea Heritage Service, Korea Heritage Agency, and K-Heritage Channel)

programme.title: Mystical Hidden Scenery: Jusanji Pond, Cheongsong EP.2
programme.desc: Completed in 1720, Jusanji Pond is fed by clear waters from Byeolbawi Rock and surrounded by lush forests of Juwangsan Mountain, creating a serene, otherworldly atmosphere. (Provided by Korea Heritage Service, Korea Heritage Agency, and K-Heritage Channel)

Sung Joon (Park Seo-joon), preocupado por Hye Jin (Hwang Jung-eum) que se lastimó con un vidrio roto, intenta preguntarle si está bien, pero Hye Jin malinterpreta su pregunta como una solicitud de dinero por romper el vidrio.

Ha Ri (Go Joon-hee) tiene algo que decirle a Hye Jin (Hwang Jung-eum), pero sigue vacilando y promete decirlo más tarde. Sung Joon se preocupa por Hye Jin mientras ella trabaja hasta tarde en la oficina.

programme.title: Ella era bonita episode 7

Ha Ri se siente incómoda al enterarse de que Hye Jin está a solas con Sung Joon durante el viaje, pero otra persona también se siente incómoda con esta situación: Shin Hyuk (Choi Si-won). En el lugar del viaje, Hye Jin y Sung Joon se encuentran en una situación inesperada.

programme.title: Ella era bonita episode 8

programme.title: El mito
programme.desc: En el 221 A.C. el primer emperador de China, Qin Shihuang, comenzó a edificar una tumba real pese a pretender ser inmortal. El mausoleo se finalizó en 37 años. La leyenda estableció que para asegurar el más absoluto secreto, todos cuantos trabajaron en el proyecto fueron enterrados en vida junto al emperador difunto. No hubo supervivientes. A lo largo de los siguientes 2.000 años, historiadores, buscadores de tumbas, y aventureros sin escrúpulos han estado buscando el tesoro real oculto en el interior. Pero nadie ha logrado localizar siquiera la entrada al mausoleo. Así, el tesoro del primer emperador, en el que se supone que está el célebre y legendario elixir de la juventud, permanece intacto.
